title: Greeting our guest
lead: The first minute or two at the table: five beats, as a conversation, not a script.

sections.name: The first minute or two
know: 1–2 minutes after seating: that’s when we approach.
Not a script a relaxed conversation instead.
Record it so the whole team can act on what you learn.

sections.name: The five beats
know: Welcome smile, eye contact, an open hand.
Last visit are they regulars or newcomers?
Dietary needs confirm with the kitchen before ordering.
The occasion shapes the pace, the comfort and a surprise.

sections.name: What to say
know: So glad you’re here: the welcome.
Allergies or dietary restrictions I should know about?
Water may I start you with water?

rows.name: Welcome
rows.meta: “Good evening, and welcome to {restaurant}. We’re so glad you’re here.”

rows.name: Last visit
rows.meta: “Have you dined with us before? When were you last with us?”

rows.name: Dietary needs
rows.meta: “Does anyone have allergies or dietary restrictions I should know about?”

rows.name: Reason for dining
rows.meta: “Are we celebrating something special tonight, or just treating yourselves?”

rows.name: Personal introduction
rows.meta: “I’m [name], and I’ll be taking care of you this evening. May I start you with water?”

keyPoints.line: after seating: that’s when we approach.
so the whole team can act on what you learn.

read.where: Approach **within the first minute or two** of seating. Follow these **five beats** in a **relaxed conversation rather than a script**, and **record what you learn** so the whole team can act on it.

keyPoints.line: smile, eye contact, an open hand.
confirm with the kitchen before ordering.
shapes the pace, the comfort and a surprise.

read.where: What we do at each beat.

stops.name: Welcome
stops.text: **Smile**, make **eye contact**, and greet the table with an **open hand**.

stops.name: Last visit
stops.text: Learn whether they are **regulars or newcomers**, including at any of **our other locations**.

stops.name: Dietary needs
stops.text: Ask **directly and calmly**; **confirm with the kitchen** before the order is placed.

stops.name: Reason for dining
stops.text: Discover the **occasion** so we can tailor **pace, seating comfort and a surprise**.

stops.name: Personal introduction
stops.text: Share **your name** and a touch of who you are; then **offer water**.

keyPoints.line: or dietary restrictions I should know about?
may I start you with water?

read.where: A guide for each beat. Keep it a **relaxed conversation rather than a script**.

sources: Baldwin Restaurant Group, The Art of Table Service: 8, Greeting Our Guest.

cards.q: When do we approach a newly seated table?
cards.answer: Within the first minute or two
wrong: Once they’ve looked at the menu
cards.source: Baldwin Restaurant Group, The Art of Table Service (service training module)

cards.q: How do we deliver the five beats?
cards.answer: As a relaxed conversation, not a script
wrong: All at once, before they sit
cards.source: Baldwin Restaurant Group, The Art of Table Service (service training module)

cards.q: Why record what you learn at the greeting?
cards.answer: So the whole team can act on it
wrong: So the manager can grade you
So the kitchen can plan prep
cards.source: Baldwin Restaurant Group, The Art of Table Service (service training module)

cards.source: Baldwin Restaurant Group, The Art of Table Service (service training module)

cards.q: Why ask the reason for dining?
cards.answer: To tailor the pace, seating comfort and a surprise
